classification.difficultyReason: Derive an unknown side and an algebraic perimeter, then evaluate with whole-number and fractional substitutions.

content.prompt: The area of the rectangle $ABCD$ is $16\text{ cm}^2$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 7 rectangle between the area statement and the statement giving BA.
spec.description: Unfilled horizontal rectangle with A bottom left, B top left, C top right and D bottom right. No side dimensions or right-angle marks. Decorative source blue is replaced by house black.
spec.mathematics: Rectangle ABCD has area 16 square centimetres; BA is x centimetres, supplied separately in editable text. Coordinates express illustrative proportions only.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the four supplied vertex labels are visible.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the length of $BC$, in terms of $x$.

answer.worked:
Divide the area by the known side length.
$$\begin{align*}BC&=\frac{\text{area}}{BA}\\BC&=\frac{16}{x}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Write down an expression for the perimeter of the rectangle, in terms of $x$.

answer.worked:
A rectangle has two sides of each length.
$$\begin{align*}P&=2\left(x+\frac{16}{x}\right)\\P&=2x+\frac{32}{x}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: If $x=4$, find the perimeter of the rectangle.

children.label: d
children.prompt: If $x=\dfrac14$, find the perimeter of the rectangle.

answer.short:
$128\dfrac12\text{ cm}$.

Substitute $x=\frac14$ into the perimeter expression.
